# Classical AI: Search and Games

**Solving problems by searching instead of learning from data: route finding, local search, constraint solving, game trees and logic, the methods behind puzzle solvers and game bots.**

Level: **Beginner** · 13 steps · 5h 32m of video · Prerequisites: [Python & Math for AI](foundations.md) (the Python part), plus comfort with lists, dictionaries and recursive functions. No machine learning needed.

## About this roadmap

Learn the search side of AI: BFS, Dijkstra, A\*, local search, constraint solving, minimax and Monte Carlo tree search, from free videos. It is the part of the field that solves problems by searching rather than by learning from data, so no machine learning is needed, but you should be comfortable with Python lists, dictionaries and recursive functions. You start with graph search and heuristics, then local search with hill climbing, simulated annealing and genetic algorithms, followed by constraint satisfaction, arc consistency and a backtracking Sudoku solver. It finishes with game playing and a lecture on propositional logic. Afterwards you can write maze solvers, puzzle solvers and simple game bots.

## Build it

- A grid maze solver with weighted cells that runs BFS, Dijkstra and A* on the same maze and prints path cost and nodes expanded for each.
- A Sudoku solver with plain backtracking and with AC-3 added, comparing how many guesses each needs on a hard puzzle.
- A Connect Four bot using minimax with alpha-beta pruning, then an MCTS version, and a script that plays them against each other.
